title: IDOR and Privilege Escalation - Profile Page

levels.low: No ownership check on GET or POST. Role field accepted from form. Any logged-in user can read or overwrite any profile and escalate any role.
levels.medium: GET checks that user_id matches the session. POST still trusts the user_id sent in the form body — override it to access another user's record.
levels.high: GET and POST both verify ownership. The role field is still accepted from the form — a user can self-promote to admin by editing their own profile.
levels.impossible: Ownership enforced on GET and POST. Role field is ignored from the form; the server always keeps the existing role. Not exploitable.

hints.low: What URL parameter controls whose profile you see? Try changing it.
hints.medium: The GET request checks the URL parameter — but what about the form submission? Look at what the POST body contains.
hints.high: You can only edit your own profile now. But is there anything in the edit form you shouldn't be able to change?
hints.impossible: Nothing to bypass. Compare vuln.py with the other levels: the role field is ignored and ownership is enforced at every step.

low.note: GET /profile?user_id=1 (admin) while logged in as a non-admin.

medium.note: POST /profile with user_id=1 in the body to overwrite admin's record.

high.note: POST to own profile with role=admin to self-promote.

impossible.note: All exploits blocked: ownership checked and role ignored.

benign.note: Legitimate role in a form update
